disease_label_per_paper: Right lower-extremity cellulitis caused by Pseudomonas putida in an immunosuppressed patient
presentation_summary: 78-year-old Japanese man with nephrotic syndrome due to membranous nephropathy, prednisolone, cyclosporine, and diabetes presented with three days of right lower-extremity pain.
Admission vitals showed temperature 37.1 degC, heart rate 91/min, blood pressure 84/53 mmHg, respiratory rate 21/min, and no impaired consciousness.
Exam showed painful swelling and warmth with punctate purpura tending to coalesce in the right lower extremity, limited to that region, without wounds or skin ulcers.
CT showed right lower-extremity swelling with fluid above the superficial fascia and no abnormal gas; exploratory incision showed no soft tissue necrosis, abscess, or odor.

Blood tests showed WBC 6.66 x10^9/L, CRP 13.37 mg/dL, BUN 33 mg/dL, creatinine 1.16 mg/dL, platelet count 128 x10^9/L, LDH 561 U/L, sodium 132 mmol/L, potassium 3.0 mmol/L, CK 340 U/L, and procalcitonin 1.01 ng/mL.
